field_body.value:
This visual story will help you plan how to get in and around the Museum of Liverpool and prepare for what you might see and do.

At National Museums Liverpool we are committed to making our museums and art galleries as inclusive and accessible as possible and so we have thought about the needs of people with a wide range of disabilities and neurodiverse conditions like Autism, Dyspraxia and ADHD.

It’s free to visit Museum of Liverpool and donations are welcome. There may be a charge for temporary exhibitions and some events.

This guide contains information about our main displays andcollections. We sometimes have to close certain rooms for maintenance, or occasionally for events.

If there is a room or object you particularly want to see, we recommend that you contact us to check that it is open or on display.

field_body_right_.value:
The museum address is:

Museum of Liverpool
Pier Head
Mann Island
Liverpool
L3 1DG

Transport

You can visit the Museum of Liverpool by bike, car, train, bus, ferry, or walking. Our website provides more details about different ways to get here: Getting to the Museum of Liverpool.

Taxis

There are suitable areas around the museum for taxi drop offs that require a short walk to the main entrance.

Accessible parking

There are six blue badge parking spaces directly opposite the museum entrance, by the Great Western Railway building. These are about 30 metres from the entrance. You will need to pre-book an accessible space before your visit. To book a space please email MoLManager@liverpoolmuseums.org.uk giving as much notice as possible, ideally at least three days. Please provide your vehicle registration, make or model and a contact phone number when requesting a space.

Guide dogs are welcome

If you plan to visit with an assistance animal other than an assistance dog, please get in touch seven days prior to your visit to discuss your request with us so we may best accommodate your visit where reasonably practicable.

Outside the main entrance you will find stone seating areas located opposite waterfront views.

field_body_right_.value:
The information desk is opposite the automatic doors. You can get information about your visit and collect tickets for Little Liverpool, the children’s gallery, which runs free timed sessions every day as well as the daily Specials, which cost £2 per child.

Fire alarms

If the fire alarm sounds please follow staff instructions and ask for assistance if required. Fire alarm tests are planned, if unexpected loud noises are a concern to you please call the museum in advance to check when the next test will take place.

Extra support for your day

We also provide the following access services to help you enjoy your day.

Please contact us ahead of your visit to ensure these are available:

  • Ear defenders
  • Two wheelchairs
  • Assistance dog water bowls

Security

Our security team will help ensure you have an enjoyable visit. We do use security measures to ensure the safety and security of all our people and collections, they are designed not to be intrusive.  If you have any concerns please don’t hesitate to contact us or speak to us in advance.

field_body_right_.value:
Floor plans

We don't currently offer printed maps for navigation however we encourage visitors to take pictures of the floor plans, located on entrance of the museum, and on the stair landing points 

You can find room guides with floor plans on our website here.

There are tactile and braille maps available on all floors.

Explore our trails

At the museum information desk, you will find a variety of interactive trails including:

  • Liverpool Black Community trail
  • Liverpool Jewish Community trail (pdf)
  • Liverpool Irish Community trail (pdf)

There is also the Disability History trail, which you can access online, including a full audio description and BSL videos.

Look out for the symbols on each trail to help you find the items included.

We have partnered with the Bottoming Podcast to create a special audio trail to explore the amazing stories behind our LGBTQ+ collections.

To access the LGBTQ+ audio trail you will require headphones and a smartphone.

Ask our staff for more information on our trails or visit our website to learn more.

Getting to the first floor

The stairs are located opposite the information desk on the ground floor.

There are 36 steps from the ground floor to the first floor. 

Every 12 steps there is a landing area.

Getting to the second floor

There are approximately 48 steps between the first and second floors, with landing places in between.

Travelling between floors by lift

There are two metal lifts available which include:

  • Tactile push button for requesting the lift
  • Inside lift buttons are tactile and include braille 
  • Enough space for one electrically powered wheelchair and one other person 
  • Mirrored back wall
  • Black flooring 
  • Single grab rail

The ground floor lift landing area is located behind the wall on the left near the entrance to the exhibition space.

The first floor lift landing area is next to History Detectives gallery.

The second floor lift landing area is within the Skylight gallery, near the entrance to the Wondrous Place gallery.

The Changing Places facilities are located within the ground floor atrium.

To gain access to the changing facilities you will need a RADAR key, it is advised to bring your own but there is one available at the information desk.

Little Liverpool encourages learning for our younger visitors through hands-on activities designed to introduce visitors to the museum, and the city of Liverpool.

Little Liverpool is suitable for accompanied children aged six and under.

There are interactives to help with sensory learning. These interactives include, but are not limited to, water play and tactile writing around the water holder.

Other facilities in Little Liverpool include:

  • Waterproof aprons
  • Dyson air blade hand dryers
  • Sanitising stations

field_body_right_.value:
Visit The Great Port gallery to discover how Liverpool transformed from a small tidal inlet into one of the world’s greatest and well-known port.

Lighting

There are low light levels within this gallery.  

  • Spotlights are used to help view the collections
  • Some information panels are backlit, which can be bright

Please take care and avoid areas with bright backlighting and spotlights if you are sensitive to light.  If you have tinted glasses it would be useful to bring them. 

Format

Many videos in The Great Port gallery have options for British Sign Language interpretation and closed captions. They include Induction Loops.

Interactives

The Great Port gallery includes some tactile displays and a sensory smell display. If you want to ensure that these interactives are available before your visit please get in touch.

field_body_right_.value:
Delve deeper into the history and archaeology of Liverpool and unearth the secrets of the city in the History Detectives gallery.

Formats

Within the History Detectives gallery there are videos which include captions, British Sign Language interpretation and Induction Loops. 

We try to ensure that these are readily available, however if there are any technical issues, please inform our staff.

Some information is placed on a red background with white text.

Most of the objects are encased with information behind glass.

Interactives

In the History Detectives gallery we offer sensory interactions that include touch. We also offer lift up/slide interactives. 

Some of our displays require you to open drawers, if you require assistance to gain full access to our interactives, please ask our staff for help.

Noise levels

The noise levels within this part of the museum can vary. Do consider bringing noise defender headphones/earbuds and be aware of the museum’s activities on the day of your visit.

When walking past the medieval Liverpool displays you may hear noise pollution coming from nearby videos. You may hear birdsong, running water and ducklings.

The Liverpool Overhead Railway gallery that tells the remarkable story of the first electric elevated railway in the world. 

Lighting

Within this area there is low lighting due to the delicate items on display, take extra care walking through. Spotlights are used to highlight information which can cause glare on text backgrounds.

Format

Most of the information is provided on a red background with white text. Some of our video interactives include Induction Loops and closed captions.

Interactives

Within The Overhead Railway gallery you will find a variety of interactives including touch screens, which often include audio handsets, captions and British Sign Language interpretation. 

We also use lift interactives to help our visitors experience ‘Journeys Through Time’.

The lighting is low with spotlights in some parts of the City Soldiers gallery.

There are a number of touch screen interactives as well as lifting and sliding interactives.

The Skylight gallery is a place for our visitors to relax and unwind. It is located on the second floor.

There is a handset audio description with information on the Liverpool Cityscape painting. This includes T-Loops.

The Skylight gallery includes two interactive screens with handheld speakers and an interactive jigsaw.

Black Lives Matter

Within this gallery you will find our statement on Black Lives Matter (BLM), for more information visit our Anti-Racism at National Museums Liverpool page.

An accessible toilet is located to the right of the entrance to the Wondrous Place gallery.  

Men’s and women’s toilets are located to the right of the entrance of The Peoples Republic gallery.

field_body_right_.value:
This part of the museum explores the experience of living in the city.

Access route and flooring

The court housing reconstruction gives visitors a chance to step back in time and view what houses used to be like in Liverpool. Please take care when entering this part of the gallery due to the uneven flooring and narrow access routes.

Lighting

Natural lighting is used throughout most of this gallery, except for the initial entrance to the gallery and the court housing reconstruction.

Format

Throughout this gallery you will find audio-visual information including closed captions, British Sign Language interpretation and induction loops.

Information in this gallery is mainly white text on a red background, with limited use of Braille.

Interactives

Within this gallery there are a variety of interactives located within the court housing reconstruction.

Noise pollution

The People’s Republic is a large gallery with high levels of noise pollution, particularly around the video displays. You may benefit from having headphones or ear buds if you are sensitive to noise.

Viewpoint

Behind the cathedral display you will see the spectacular views of Liverpool’s Liver Birds. This is a great spot to take a break, however there is limited seating within this area.

Trigger warning

If you follow to the left once having entered the gallery you will come across an audio-visual of war footage. Visitors can hear gun fire, high pitch whistles and shouting. These sounds can be heard within other areas of the gallery. There are scenes of deceased soldiers. If you think someone within your visiting group may be affected by this, please use the access route to right of the gallery entrance.

field_body_right_.value:
The Wondrous Place gallery celebrates the city’s successful entertainers, musicians, sports people, writers, poets, visual artists and comedians.

There are four parts to this gallery which include:

  • Liverpool on screen
  • Music in Liverpool
  • Games in Liverpool
  • Sports in Liverpool

This gallery is located on the second floor and includes a handset audio description at the entrance which includes a T-Loop. This has information on the gallery.

Lighting

There is natural light throughout the gallery, however when entering Wondrous Place and within the two movie rooms lights are turned down to make the viewing of screens easier.

Noise

Please note that throughout this gallery there are screens playing clips, noise coming from interactives and overhead music. Noise levels increase during busy periods. Please bring noise cancelling headphones or earbuds if you think this will impact your visit.

Trigger warning

Please be aware that topics of football racism, drugs, Hillsborough, guns and gang violence are mentioned in this gallery.

Seating

Throughout the gallery there are wooden benches for visitors to rest on. This includes a bench at a viewing point by the window where you can take in the views of the River Mersey.

Format

The majority of the information is text based and often includes white writing on a pink or red background. There are braille labels accompanying the iconic album covers display, which includes tactile images.

Interactives

There are different interactives available in the Wondrous Place gallery, including a music quiz, lift up and tactile interactions, sing-along interactions in the karaoke booth and a chance to play video games developed by Liverpool games studios.

To avoid disappointment please ring ahead to check if specific interactives are working.

Video rooms

The Wondrous Place gallery celebrates the city’s successful entertainers, musicians, sports people, writers, poets, visual artists and comedians.

There are four parts to this gallery which include:

  • Liverpool on screen
  • Music in Liverpool
  • Games in Liverpool
  • Sports in Liverpool

This gallery is located on the second floor and includes a handset audio description at the entrance which includes a T-Loop. This has information on the gallery.

Lighting

There is natural light throughout the gallery, however when entering Wondrous Place and within the two movie rooms lights are turned down to make the viewing of screens easier.

Noise

Please note that throughout this gallery there are screens playing clips, noise coming from interactives and overhead music. Noise levels increase during busy periods. Please bring noise cancelling headphones or earbuds if you think this will impact your visit.

Trigger warning

Please be aware that topics of football racism, drugs, Hillsborough, guns and gang violence are mentioned in this gallery.

Seating

Throughout the gallery there are wooden benches for visitors to rest on. This includes a bench at a viewing point by the window where you can take in the views of the River Mersey.

Format

The majority of the information is text based and often includes white writing on a pink or red background. There are braille labels accompanying the iconic album covers display, which includes tactile images.

Interactives

There are different interactives available in the Wondrous Place gallery, including a music quiz, lift up and tactile interactions, sing-along interactions in the karaoke booth and a chance to play video games developed by Liverpool games studios.
